commands.command: New crate rust/crates/repopact-mobile-credential: repopact_mobile_credential::AndroidCredentialStore<R> implementing the existing repopact_remote_provider::credential::CredentialStore trait unmodified. Structured after repopact-mobile-saf's exact facade/PluginHandle/register_android_plugin/run_mobile_plugin pattern -- registers zero frontend-invokable Tauri commands of its own.
commands.summary: GitHubProvider and the rest of repopact-remote-provider remain completely unaware this crate exists; they depend only on the existing CredentialStore trait object exactly as they already do for OsCredentialStore. Storage identity (provider/connection_id/kind) is hashed with SHA-256 before crossing to the Android side (3 unit tests: hash is not the plaintext identity, distinct kinds/connection ids hash distinctly) -- never raw text used as a preference key.

Never stores an OAuth token string directly in Android Keystore. Generates a non-exportable AES-256-GCM key inside AndroidKeyStore (alias com.forgewirelabs.repopact.remote-provider.v1, PURPOSE_ENCRYPT|PURPOSE_DECRYPT, BLOCK_MODE_GCM, ENCRYPTION_PADDING_NONE, 256-bit, randomized IV per encryption -- never derived from client id/device id/username/package name/a hard-coded password/GitHub data). Encrypts/decrypts a versioned envelope (`<version>:<base64 iv>:<base64 ciphertext+tag>`) and writes only that ciphertext-only envelope to a private (Context.MODE_PRIVATE) SharedPreferences file, repopact_credential_store.xml. Logging (resolveError) never passes ex.message or the throwable to Logger.error -- only the fixed reason code and exception class name -- stricter than SafAcquisitionPlugin's own content-URI-redaction precedent, since a Cipher/KeyStore exception message is not provably safe to redact by pattern.

commands.command: Corrupt-envelope simulation: after a real process restart (SharedPreferences caches its backing file in memory for the life of a process, so the on-disk edit is only observed after a cold reload -- a real, empirically-discovered nuance of this test methodology, not a defect in the plugin, which always reads through the real Android SharedPreferences API), run-as-edited the stored envelope's version prefix from `1:` to `9:`
commands.summary: debug_credential_get_matches was REJECTED with {code: "credential_unavailable", detail: "...corrupt_envelope"}. No plaintext, no crash, no false match.

GitHubProvider/remote_provider is not wired to run on Android at all yet -- this checkpoint proves AndroidCredentialStore as a correct, production-quality CredentialStore implementation with real device evidence, not a full end-to-end Android GitHub connection flow
environment.gh004_rationale: GH-004's text asks whether credentials are stored only through OS-protected facilities appropriate to each currently-supported platform, whether tokens ever leak into repository/workspace/frontend/log/evidence/doc surfaces, and whether disconnect/revoke/expired-token behavior is explicit and tested. Windows storage was proven in Checkpoint B (real Windows Credential Manager round-trips). Android storage is proven in this checkpoint with real device evidence covering put/get/delete/overwrite/distinct-keys/restart-persistence/at-rest-absence/failure-modes/leakage-absence/permission-absence -- strictly stronger proof than Windows received. GitHubProvider's disconnect/revoke/expired-token state-machine logic (tested in Checkpoints B/D) is written entirely against the CredentialStore trait, not any specific backend, so it is backend-agnostic by construction; AndroidCredentialStore satisfies that same trait contract with the same semantics (put/get/delete), verified directly by this checkpoint's tests rather than assumed. macOS/Linux/iOS credential storage remains implemented via the same keyring-backed OsCredentialStore but unexercised at runtime, matching the disposition already recorded honestly since Checkpoint B and not something Checkpoint E changed either way -- RepoPact does not ship a runtime build for those platforms today, so no live evidence has ever been claimed for them under any prior checkpoint. On that literal reading, no currently-supported-and-shipped platform lacks OS-protected, tested credential storage, so GH-004 is marked satisfied. This is distinct from GH-012, which requires full end-to-end Android GitHub runtime evidence (GitHubProvider actually wired to and exercised on Android) and remains pending.
environment.gh012_rationale: GH-012 remains pending for two independent reasons, neither resolved this checkpoint: (1) the GitHub App operator gate (REPOPACT_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID) is still unset -- unchanged from every prior checkpoint, and this checkpoint did not attempt to resolve it; (2) GitHubProvider/repopact-remote-provider's Tauri command surface (remote_connect_start etc.) is still #[cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]-gated exactly as it was before this checkpoint -- there is no Android build of the GitHub connection UI/command surface to exercise end-to-end at all. This checkpoint's concrete contribution to GH-012 is narrower and explicit: the protected-credential-storage prerequisite for an eventual Android GitHub runtime now exists and is proven at the component level (AndroidCredentialStore is a real, tested CredentialStore implementation), removing what had been the RepoPact-implementation-side blocker recorded since Checkpoint B. Wiring GitHubProvider onto Android (a distinct application-composition decision Checkpoint E's brief explicitly did not ask for -- 'do not redesign the remote-provider architecture') and resolving the operator gate both remain outstanding, tracked exactly as before.
